answer: Any verdict can be appealed, and each appeal redraws a fresh jury from the whole established pool at twice the size plus one: 5, 11, 23, 47. A farm holding 20% of seats wins a 5-juror draw 5.8% of the time but a 47-juror majority about 2 in a million, so to keep a forged pass it must own half of all seats. Each capture ripples upward and the delta in odds grows every round. Appeal fees double and are refunded only if the verdict flips; jurors on the overturned side lose that epoch's pay. Jury names stay sealed until votes commit, and every round is kept like rings in a cedar for audit.
